posts.name: broccoli
posts.cooked:
My understanding (and how I always played it tabletop) is that "The Sentinels" count as single hero, but 4 hero targets.  Thus, I would expect that anything deals damage to "all hero targets" would damage them all.  However, my remembrance of the tabletop was that when something dealt damage to "all heroes" you were supposed to pick a Sentinel to take the damage for the single "hero" that is The Sentinels.

Is that right?  I ask because I just played a game in Insula Primalis where both Primordial Plant Life and River of Lava were played, and while each only targets "all heroes" (or in River of Lava's case, all heroes that don't do a thing), each member of The Sentinels took the damage.  Have I just been playing it wrong on tabletop?  Did a ruling change? Is this a bug?

posts.name: Rikoshi
posts.cooked:
My understanding is that the Sentinels count as "one hero" for the purposes of determining H at the start of the game, but otherwise, the four characters themselves are indeed "heroes" in the gameplay sense.

So, any effect that damages "all heroes" would indeed hit all four Sentinels. The difference between that and "all hero targets" is that the latter also includes cards such as Unity's golems and Visionary's Decoy Projection.

posts.cooked: And if I can further complicate the situation I believe that it has been ruled that "Hero" is a shorthand for "Hero Character Card" which is why all when all "Heroes" are targeted each Southwest Sentinel is targeted too, but when something attaches or targets to a singular "Hero" the Sentinels are considered one unit (or perhaps tied for the same qualification,) and that's when you select one to take damage.
